We had a great discussion around the council table, certainly in terms of what was being proposed. And I'm recommending the council goes forward with the OP and zoning updates. There are a number of changes to or modifications to the proposed policy from what we looked at in December. And I'm just going to quickly go over them. I'm not proposing to amend the OPA wording. That's pretty basic. I am proposing that we amend the definition for secondary dwelling units. So a secondary dwelling unit in the bylaw here is a unit within an existing house. So the previous wording, and you'll see we have the track changes in the accompanying report that associated, that came along with the report and that's what I'm reading for. The previous definition was, that had the sharing two of at least, sharing at least two of the following with the principal dwelling unit was fairly prescriptive. It's something that I'm used to in working with other zoning bylaws. However, we heard loud and clear from the community as well that we want the preferences, the policies to be less prescriptive and more flexible. And I'd also discussed the implementation with our chief building official, who also feels that the proposed wording that we now have is easier to administer from the perspective of the constructing a continuous fire separation. So we're proposing to modify the wording to simply state that a secondary dwelling unit is a separate permanent self-contained unit, which is subordinate in size and located in the same building as the principal dwelling unit of a single detached, semi-detached or townhouse dwelling. Its creation does not result in the creation of a semi-detached or duplex dwelling. So we're also proposing a modification to the definition of a detached, of a second dwelling, which is a detached dwelling on its own. So the modification proposed that favors modular homes which are built under controlled conditions in factories and assembled on foundations on a site. And while they can resemble manufactured or mobile homes, they would be built according to Ontario building code standards and have a longer life expectancy. And this is a policy approach that's consistent with the other municipal zoning bylaws I've worked with. So through the official plan review, our consultant planner supported a general policy approach as a modular home holds its value as same as a conventional stick built house and is a good investment for those seeking affordable housing as it does not depreciate. So we are seeking council's, that was flagged for attention from council. So we are seeking council's direction on that particular item. I'll go now into the proposal for the general provisions, the parking, the amendment to section 3.16, the parking requirements. So that's just a little technical modification to better align us with the proposed, well, with the Planning Act requirements of allowing tandem parking. That doesn't have a whole lot of practical effect, but it is a technical item that we've included in there. With the, to section 3.19, the secondary dwelling unit or second dwelling shall comply with the provisions of the Building Code Act. I'm not proposing any change there, but I am just advising that the minimum dwelling size requirements under the code do vary based on orientation and configuration of the amenities and rooms of the dwelling. And they can be fairly, so these dwellings, coach houses, tiny homes, whatever you call them can be very small. And I think a challenge I had and probably planners across the board when people were asking us about tiny homes and we'd ask our chief building official, so how small will the building code allow you to build? And there's no easy answer to that. It depends on a whole bunch of variables. So that's why, and it depends on the type of home. Further down that page, additional provisions for second dwellings. I'm proposing a very small amendment there, just we know that an accessory building may be constructed as a second dwelling provided it complies with all applicable zoning provisions for the principal dwelling. And I've just highlighted excluding dwelling unit size. That doesn't change the practical effect of what we've been talking about, but we always, the above provision allows a secondary dwelling to be an accessory building to be a lot smaller than the original and as small as the code will allow it. So that just confirms that intent. The second last bullet point there, a second dwelling shall comply with the height limits for an accessory building, except for the second dwelling is located in a settlement area. And I've also added the, when a lot is less than 0.2 hectares or half an acre in size, in which case it would be limited to a height of one story. So on a larger lot, we feel that there'd be less of a need for those more restrictive provisions and that was in response to a comment from Councilor Carroll and a very valid point. The final proposed modification is relating to servicing. So the direction we've had from council previously is that you wanted to see the second dwelling be located close enough to the main buildings that it's really clearly and truly accessory. So then we were looking at how close is too close. And we threw a 30 meters down as a number, but that's a bit of an arbitrary number and also a fairly low number.
